summary: The shared four-dot row is visually consistent across platforms: green, peach, gray, and cyan dots have matching alignment, size, and dark outlines.
Android adds a lower state row with a pink outlined dot followed by large dark text reading "Waiting pulse"; React has no corresponding element.
The Android waiting-pulse row is fully visible within the component bounds, with no apparent clipping; the shared headers, borders, and crop dimensions otherwise match.
likelyCauses: Android renders a waiting/pulse state that React's state mapping or conditional rendering omits.
The platform implementations use different default state sets or fixtures.
cases.suggestedOwner: Status Dot component owner with Android implementation support
suggestedFixes: If React is the baseline contract, remove or disable the waiting/pulse state in the Android fixture and rerun the visual test.
If the waiting-pulse state is intended, add the equivalent pink dot and label to React and match its typography, spacing, and alignment.
Use a shared state fixture and verify the state row at identical coordinates within the 342×92 component bounds.

summary: Bottom row skeleton placeholder (circle + bar) is vertically clipped/missing in the Android view, whereas React shows the full row.
The Android content stack appears shifted slightly upward, pushing the bottom row past the 150px canvas boundary.
Circle stroke weight on the Android side appears marginally heavier in the bottom circle compared to React.
likelyCauses: Android layout does not respect the fixed 150px canvas height and lets the content stack overflow the bottom edge.
Vertical spacing or row heights in the Android skeleton differ from React, compressing the stack.
Inset/padding values for skeleton rows are inconsistent between platforms.
suggestedFixes: Constrain the Android skeleton container to the same 150px height as the React fixture and clip/contain overflowing rows.
Align vertical gaps and row heights to the React spec; verify skeleton block paddings match token values.
Re-run the visual diff with the overflow region excluded to confirm residual mismatch is within tolerance.
Audit the bottom skeleton row bounds to ensure the circle and bar render within the canvas without being cut.
intentional: Vertical content overflow within the fixed 150px canvas mirrors CSS behavior on the React side and is documented as an intentional platform-difference (UiSkeletonVisualContent); not a defect on either platform.

summary: Android card typography is narrower and lighter; React uses a wider, monospaced-looking treatment for both text lines.
Android cards are visibly shorter, leaving larger inter-card and bottom spacing.
The Android unselected card uses a pale green-tinted fill and light-gray border, while React uses a white fill, black border, and hard black shadow.
The Android selected fill is muted green-gray instead of React's brighter light-cyan fill.
Card widths and right insets differ slightly, and Android text begins slightly higher within each card.
likelyCauses: Platform-specific font-family, weight, and letter-spacing values
Different card min-height or vertical padding on Android
Unmapped state-specific surface, border, and shadow tokens
Android selected-state color token does not match the React cyan
cases.suggestedOwner: Android design-system or SurfaceListItem component owner
suggestedFixes: Align Android typography with React by matching font family, size, weight, line height, and letter spacing.
Match the React card height, stack gap, text padding, and horizontal insets within the 1dp layout tolerance.
Use the baseline white fill, black border, and hard shadow for the unselected state.
Update the Android selected fill to the baseline bright light-cyan color while retaining the matching black border and shadow.
Re-run the component-bounds comparison after verifying both normal and selected state tokens.

summary: The React viewport is blank, while Android renders a complete notification-center card in the upper portion of the screen.
React is missing the NOTIFICATIONS header, the "2 items" count, both notification rows, warning/info icons, message typography, and View/Open/Dismiss controls.
Android uses an off-white background, heavy black card and button borders, and a hard black offset shadow; these component surfaces are absent on React.
The Android card is approximately 310×270 px at x=22–331 and y=86–357; React has no corresponding component bounds.
likelyCauses: The React notification-center component is unmounted or hidden by a failed conditional.
React is using a different route or initialization state and never reaches the populated two-item state.
The React notification data binding is empty or unavailable, causing the populated UI to be skipped.
The React baseline may have captured the wrong element or a blank application root.
cases.suggestedOwner: React Home and notification-center feature owner
suggestedFixes: Render the populated notification-center component in React for the same state shown on Android.
Supply both notification records and derive the header count from the rendered item list.
Match Android's card bounds, header, row spacing, icon treatments, typography, button sizes, borders, colors, and offset shadow.
Recapture React against the actual notification-center bounds after restoring the component.

summary: Android omits React's dark-separated ACTIONS section and full-width red "Remove Member" button.
Description and role states differ: React shows "Owner" as the description and role, while Android shows a description sentence and a "Member" role badge.
React uses thick dark-gray section separators; Android uses thin light-gray separators, changing the visible section bounds and spacing.
Android's main profile avatar and person icon are larger with a heavier stroke, and its "No created agents" text is upright rather than italic.
The header-right icon differs: React shows a person/plus symbol, while Android shows a speech-bubble shape.
likelyCauses: Android conditionally omits the actions block or fails to enable it for an owner role.
Description and role fields are populated from different data or fallback states across platforms.
Android divider tokens use a different color and thickness from the shared design.
Avatar sizing, icon stroke, and empty-state font-style tokens are not mapped consistently.
The Android toolbar uses the wrong icon resource.
suggestedFixes: Render the ACTIONS heading and red full-width "Remove Member" button with React-equivalent bounds, or hide them on both platforms.
Align the description and role values, and restore React's help icon beside the Role label.
Use the same divider color and stroke thickness throughout all profile sections.
Match React's main avatar size, icon proportions, and italic empty-state typography.
Replace the Android speech-bubble icon with the React person/plus icon.
